description:
Today, the UK and EU have agreed three new deals on food exports, youth mobility and emissions at a summit in Brussels. However, no agreement has been reached over the question of tuition fees after the EU demanded the UK agree to cut tuition costs for European students. So what impact will this sticking point have on the deal?  

With the conversation around UK’s relationship with the European Union back in the spotlight, that can only mean one thing. The Brexitcast gang are back together. Adam is joined by Laura in the studio, and Chris and Katya are in Brussels, to unpack the day’s events.

author: BBC News
description:
Delegates at the UN climate summit, COP31, are deadlocked over a draft agreement that makes no mention of phasing out fossil fuels, and admits that the world has failed to keep global warming within 1.5 degrees Celsius of pre-industrial levels. 

This year's COP, in Antalya, Turkey, has revived questions about the efficacy of big climate summits, particularly as the United States - one of the world's largest fossil fuel producers - is not attending. President Donald Trump officially withdrew the US from the Paris Climate Agreement on his return to the White House.  

In this video, our climate editor tells us why it's been so difficult to reach a consensus at COP31, and we ask our correspondent whether the entire COP model is broken.

description:
The UK and EU have agreed a new deal covering food exports, carbon emission and a new youth mobility scheme allowing 100,000 young Britons to work, volunteer, study or travel in Europe.
 
President of the European Council António Costa said the EU remains open to the "closest possible relationship" with the UK while UK prime minister Burnham says it's a "historic moment" as people in the UK "want a better deal" with the European Union.
 
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has insisted the new deal between the EU and UK "isn't fair" while Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has argued the new deal will see "vastly more red tape piled on British businesses".

author: BBC News
description:
Warning: This story discusses sexual violence and abuse,
 
A woman who was drugged, raped and advertised for sex online by her husband has said she will "never feel completely safe" after four men were found guilty of sexually abusing her, in the first trial of its kind in England.
 
Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, said: "The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way."
 
Philip Young, 50, had already pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and raping his wife over a 13-year period at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire. He invited men via websites and apps such as Craigslist, Grindr and Fab Swingers to the couple's home without her knowledge.

author: BBC News
description:
Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region.
 
Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.
 
Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022.
 
In an interview with the BBC, former Nato Deputy Supreme Allied Commander Richard Shirreff described the missile as a "deliberate attack" on Poland.

A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers across major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned.

Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.

In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK.

The world watched a historical trilateral meeting between Russia, China and the US this week. 

Following the summit in Shenzhen, the countries issued a joint declaration, vowing dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and reforming the UN, and saying they plan to increase supplies of petroleum products.
 
Despite the rhetoric and imagery, the joint statement from the three countries provided minimal substance.
 
BBC's Steve Lai walks us through the meeting and how the new "Big Three" may imagine a new world order.

author: BBC News
description:
A 12-year-old boy is killed by a speeding driver. What follows is a two-year fight for justice by his family. 

Keaton Slater died in the collision on Coventry’s Radford Road on June 14, 2024. His death unites the city and spurs his family to do all they can to ensure his killer is put behind bars.

But Aleksanders Dolars evaded capture for more than two years by fleeing to Latvia. 

He was finally brought to justice following a determined campaign by Keaton’s parents Louise and Clint. But even after sentencing, the family’s fight is not over.
